summary: Botetourt County, VA: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a tower as gone; a 1965 trail shelter stands on the summit, with reported footings nearby.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone. A trail shelter stands on the summit; the lookout's footings are reported, but the lookout's history is not documented in the sources found.

access.note: On foot from the Appalachian Trail by a short side trail to the shelter.

visit.trail_note: The side trail to the shelter is about 0.10 miles from the AT, easy, with little climbing.

events.note: The Roanoke Appalachian Trail Club built the trail shelter on the summit. The shelter is not the lookout itself.

evidence.supports: the summit is the eastern peak of Fullhart Mountain, also known as Fullhardt Mountain
evidence.quote: this is the eastern peak of Fullhart Mountain, also known as Fullhardt Mountain

evidence.supports: the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a tower as gone in Botetourt County
footings of the former fire tower are in the shelter area
evidence.quote: The footings of the former fire tower are in the shelter area at the top of the hill.

evidence.supports: the writer found almost nothing about the lookout's history and doubted it was built
evidence.quote: As for the lookout, I have found almost nothing about the history nor can I find it shown on any maps.

evidence.supports: the footings look new and the writer wondered whether a lookout was built
evidence.quote: These footings look so new, with no evidence yet, I wonder if a lookout was even built.

evidence.supports: shelter built by the Roanoke Appalachian Trail Club in 1965
evidence.quote: The shelter was built by the Roanoke Appalachian Trail Club in 1965.

evidence.supports: the shelter stands on the summit
evidence.quote: On the summit is the Fullhart Knob shelter.

shelter listing gives 1965 as the build date
the shelter sits on the site of a former fire tower, per a hiker's blog
evidence.quote: The shelter is located on the site of a former fire tower.

evidence.supports: short side trail to the shelter is easy with little climbing
evidence.quote: The short side trail to the shelter area is easy, not climbing much elevation.

the shelter's cistern, the last on the AT to use one
evidence.quote: This is the last shelter on the Appalachian Trail to use a rain cistern.

sources.title: Fullhart Knob East Peak Lookout Site
Appalachian Trail to Fulhardt Knob Shelter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list and WillhiteWeb use Fullhart; the RATC shelter listing and some hiking pages use Fullhardt. The record keeps Fullhart Knob.
WillhiteWeb says the footings belong to the former fire tower, then doubts a lookout was ever built. The story reports both views and does not settle the question.

notes_for_editor: Built date, builder of the lookout, and fate are not documented. The 1965 date is for the trail shelter, not the lookout. The one site visitor says footings are present, then doubts a lookout was built; the hiker blog repeats the former-tower claim without a source. Brief status (gone), county and coordinates match FFLA. Searches used: 2. Pages read: 5 including the FFLA list.
